referents.why: 'Your loins': the possessive of the command's addressee, the one told to gird up, who is Job.
Object of 'I will ask', second person, inside the LORD's speech: the one addressed, Job.
First person 'make known to me' inside the LORD's speech: the speaker, the LORD. The builder's 'cl1s' is a slot id, not a candidate.
Implied second person subject of the imperative 'gird up': the one the command is spoken to, Job.
Implied first person subject of 'I will ask you': the LORD speaking. The builder's 'cl1s' is a slot id, not a candidate.
Implied second person subject of the imperative 'make known to me': Job, the one commanded to speak.

links.why: A waw joining a command to a change of person (gird up / I will ask) is 'so that' by the link rule, not a plain 'and'.
links.category: command joined to change of person

links.why: Command, then waw + yiqtol in a different person: the questioning is what the girding is for.
A waw joining an imperative to a change of person (first person 'I will ask' to second person 'make known') is 'so that' by the link rule.
links.category: command joined to change of person

links.why: The answer is what the questioning is for, the same rule as the first link of this verse.
links.category: command joined to change of person

groups.why: The builder put cl1 as 'part', which is not an imperative member role. cl1 is what the command is for, so it is 'aim'.
The builder's sender 'cl1s' is a slot. The speaker of 'I will question you' is the LORD. Addressee added: Job.
groups.category: speaker and addressee of a turn

cant_tell.what: Whether 'you shall inform Me' (cl2) is the purpose of the questioning or a second demand in the same speech.
cant_tell.why: Both readings fit the waw. The purpose type is chosen because the link rule gives it for a command after a change of person; the form does not settle the sense.
